- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 11371 (`_std_rtr_stall_secs=$(( STALL_THRESHOLD_MINUTES * 60 ))`)
  Problem: The standalone stall recovery path (`run_standalone_stall_recovery` function's `retrigger_review` case) still computes its in-flight review freshness window from `STALL_THRESHOLD_MINUTES` (120m) rather than `REVIEW_RUN_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES` (250m). The orchestrator-managed equivalent at line 9353 was correctly updated to `_rtr_stall_secs=$(( REVIEW_RUN_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES * 60 ))`. The standalone path's inline jq filter at lines 11373-11401 therefore classifies any review run aged 120-250 minutes as a zombie and drops it from `_std_rtr_inflight_id`, falling through to the `_direct_inflight_review_run_on_branch` fallback at line 11412.
  Why it fails at runtime: Normally the `_direct_inflight_review_run_on_branch` fallback catches this case — that function was correctly updated to use `REVIEW_RUN_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES` at line 8456. But the function's documented contract (lines 8440-8443) explicitly tolerates fail-open on any `gh`/`jq`/`date` error. When the direct fallback also fails open and returns empty, the inline guard's stale 120m threshold means the empty-commit push at lines 11420+ proceeds under a still-editing review run at 120-250 minutes, tripping `AUTOFIX_PRE_EDITOR_STALE_BASE -> soft_exit` and discarding the review pass. This is the exact regression the PR fixes for the orchestrator-managed path, but it remains present in the standalone path. The standalone path is gated by `ENABLE_STANDALONE_STALL_RECOVERY` (default `true`), so this path is active by default for any non-orchestrator issue that stalls in `ai:done`.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 11414 (`(fresh, <${STALL_THRESHOLD_MINUTES}m)`)
  Problem: The standalone path's log message still interpolates `STALL_THRESHOLD_MINUTES` instead of `REVIEW_RUN_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES`. The orchestrator-managed equivalent at line 9388 correctly uses `<${REVIEW_RUN_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES}m>`. When the cached scan successfully finds the run and this log fires, it reports a freshness window of 120m when the direct fallback (which is the authoritative check) uses 250m. This is an observability inconsistency rather than a correctness defect, since this branch only fires when the cached scan already found the run (meaning the push was blocked regardless).
  Why it fails at runtime: No runtime failure — log-only inconsistency that would mislead operators comparing standalone vs. orchestrator-managed stall-recovery traces.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

The orchestrator-managed equivalent at line 9353 was correctly updated to `_rtr_stall_secs=$(( REVIEW_RUN_MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES * 60 ))`. Line 11414 still interpolates `${STALL_THRESHOLD_MINUTES}`. No diff hunk in the PR touches lines 11371 or 11414. `_direct_inflight_review_run_on_branch` (line 8456) and `build_active_issue_set` (lines 8502, 8526) were correctly updated. The standalone `retrigger_review` inline guard — the fourth review-run freshness site implementing the same pattern — was missed.

The existing standalone tests (`test_standalone_retrigger_review_skips_empty_commit_when_review_run_has_blank_head_branch_but_matching_sha` at line 5985, `test_standalone_conflict_sweep_consumes_budget_after_override_cap` at line 5943) do not test the review-run freshness window at all. - File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 8468-8471 (`_direct_inflight_review_run_on_branch` function's jq filter)
  Problem: The direct-inflight fallback helper only matches review runs by `.name` / `.workflowName` and does not check `.path`. The cached scan and inline guards check both name and path (for `ai-review.yml`, `internal-review.yml`, `review_autofix.yml`), but this helper's jq filter only checks:
```jq
((.name // "") == "AI Review" or (.name // "") == "Internal Review" or (.name // "") == "Review Autofix")
or ((.workflowName // "") == "AI Review" or (.workflowName // "") == "Internal Review" or (.workflowName // "") == "Review Autofix")
```
Missing the `.path` clause that the other guards have. If a consumer renames the display name AND the path-based match fails in the cached scan, the direct-inflight fallback will also miss the run.
  Why it fails at runtime: The helper can fail to detect a legitimate in-progress review run when the workflow display name has been changed in the consumer repo, allowing the empty-commit push to proceed and clobber live review work.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
